title: Check the search reports, workflows and event subscriptions before the November automation go-live
situation: Kestrel Ridge Logistics is about to switch on its joiner, mover and leaver automation in SailPoint Identity Security Cloud (ISC). A colleague built 12 search queries, 5 scheduled search reports, 8 workflows and 10 event trigger subscriptions in a hurry before going on leave. Some queries were typed with lowercase operators or a missing bracket, one report goes to a person who has left, several workflows were never tested, and nobody is sure which subscriptions will actually receive which events.
your_task: Run every search query against the 10 identities and record which identities it returns, or why ISC Search would reject it.
Decide for each scheduled search report whether the next run sends an email, skips an empty result, or cannot be sent.

Validate every workflow from its scrambled list of steps: one trigger first, both branches of every choice operator connected, every path ending in an end step, and every variable coming from an earlier step.
Work out which subscriptions fire for each of the 7 sample events, and explain every subscription that is disabled, filtered out or has a broken filter.
Write down the step order of each valid, single-path workflow for the run book.
why_it_matters: A search typed with a lowercase 'and' quietly returns far more people than intended, and a report that nobody receives hides leavers who still have access. A workflow with a dead end or a missing branch fails halfway through a leaver process, and a subscription filter with a typo means the ticketing system never hears about a termination. These mistakes are cheap to catch before go-live and expensive after.
done_when: All 12 queries are marked MATCHES (with the identities), NO_MATCH or INVALID_QUERY with the reason.
All 5 scheduled reports are marked SEND_REPORT, SKIP_EMPTY or NOT_SENT with the reason.
All 8 workflows are marked VALID or with their first error, and the run order of the valid single-path workflows is written down.
Every event lists the subscriptions that fire, and every non-firing subscription has a reason.

glossary.Identity Security Cloud (ISC): SailPoint's software-as-a-service identity governance platform, formerly called IdentityNow.
glossary.Search query: A text query such as attributes.department:Finance AND attributes.location:London that ISC Search runs against identities and other indexed data.
glossary.Nested query: A query inside @accounts(...) or @access(...) whose conditions must all be true of the same account or access item.
glossary.Scheduled search: A saved search that runs on a schedule and emails its results to chosen recipients.
glossary.Event trigger: A platform event such as Identity Created or Provisioning Completed that ISC publishes to subscribed services and workflows.
glossary.JavaScript Object Notation Path (JSONPat: A small language for selecting parts of a JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) document; ISC uses it for event trigger subscription filters.
glossary.Workflow: A no-code automation in ISC that starts from one trigger and runs actions and operators until an end step.
glossary.Choice operator: A workflow step such as Compare Strings that sends the run down a true path or a false path.

talking_point: Reviewed Kestrel Ridge's ISC automation before go-live: of 12 search queries, 8 matched, 1 matched nobody and 3 were rejected (a lowercase 'and', an unknown attribute and a missing bracket), and one forgotten operator silently widened a query to 4 people; 2 of 5 scheduled reports will send, 1 skips its empty result and 2 cannot be sent (one because its only recipient has left, one because of a lowercase 'and'); 3 of 8 workflows were valid while 5 had a missing branch, a dead end, two triggers or variables used before they exist; and the 7 sample events produced 8 subscription deliveries, with one subscription never firing because its filter used '=' instead of '=='.
